thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sustained 429 spike for tenant HarborBank in vpc-harbor-usw2 (dedicated pool hb-prod-pool). 30s avg 429 rate = 18% (baseline <1%).

sam: Confirmed from logs — client-side retries + backlog. Not seeing backend 5xx. Looks like fairshare enforcement kicking in on the pool.

lia: @sam grabbing oncall. I’m on it. First pass: check pool utilization, queue lengths, and any noisy tenants.

mike: I can see backlog on the serving runtime KV cache build jobs — some long prefix requests are hammering token generation. Might be a small set of tenants creating long context requests.

hana: CS — HarborBank is in heavy realtime use for fraud scoring. They just rolled a new integration. Need ETA/impact message for SRE and Sales.

tara: Sales here — HarborBank is on an enterprise contract; if this is our fault we might need a short-term contract override/waiver for rate penalties. Need details on scope and duration.

jess: From model runtime metrics: request latencies are normal, token throughput per-host saturated due to continuous batching queue growth. Fairshare algorithm is reducing their token allowance -> 429s.

sam: Quick triage commands I ran:
```
# pool summary
rbctl pool get hb-prod-pool --region us-west-2
rbctl pool nodes hb-prod-pool --json | jq '.[] | {id,util,tenants}'
```
Top noisy tenant is hb-internal-a, but HarborBank traffic maps to tenant harborbank-prod.

kube-bot: Deployments in hb-prod-pool: 42 containers, 8 nodes at 96% GPU util. Autoscaler: max=8 nodes, current=8. No pending scale-up.

lia: Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Temporary fairshare bump for harborbank-prod (increase weight) — quick but impacts others.
2) Emergency burst capacity: add 2 nodes to hb-prod-pool (requires infra quota override).
3) Route HarborBank requests to a compatible fallback model on a different pool (latency tradeoff).
4) Identify and throttle noisy tenant hb-internal-a (if safe).

mike: I prefer 1 + 4: bump HarborBank weight by 2x for 1 hour and reduce noisy tenant to min weight. That avoids infra provisioning delays.

sam: Actionable commands (if we go 1):
```
rbctl fairshare adjust --pool hb-prod-pool --tenant harborbank-prod --weight 200 --duration 3600
rbctl fairshare adjust --pool hb-prod-pool --tenant hb-internal-a --weight 10 --duration 3600
```
Applying now will take effect within 30s.

lia: @mike can you confirm side effects? jess, any eval regressions expected from weight bump?

jess: No model change. Just servicing more tokens for that tenant. Latency SLAs for others may degrade slightly but within tolerances if we only do 1 hour. Monitor token queues.

hana: I'll draft a brief customer message: "We're mitigating an upstream rate control event affecting your production cluster by temporarily increasing capacity allocation. Expect reduced 429s within minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and post-mortem." Send me the ETA once changes are live.

tara: I'll notify the HarborBank account exec with the same note and loop legal if contract language needed.

lia: Ok executing option 1+4 now. Will post when commands complete.

sam: Running commands...
```
# apply fairshare bump
rbctl fairshare adjust --pool hb-prod-pool --tenant harborbank-prod --weight 200 --duration 3600
rbctl fairshare adjust --pool hb-prod-pool --tenant hb-internal-a --weight 10 --duration 3600
```

kube-bot: fairshare update: harborbank-prod weight=200 (applied), hb-internal-a weight=10 (applied).

lia: Changes applied. Monitoring token error rate...

(2m later) sam: 429 rate down to 2.4% in 60s window. Queue lengths decreasing.

hana: Sending customer note now. ETA in portal set to "Mitigation in progress — monitoring".

tara: HarborBank replied: "Thanks. We're seeing fewer errors. Please confirm you will follow up with a post-mortem." They've paused the new integration roll for 30m.

lia: Good catch. Follow-ups:
- (sam) Open INC ticket linking to fairshare adjust, attach logs and commands.
- (jess/mike) Investigate root cause: why fairshare enforced so aggressively (prefix lengths? caching?).
- (eng-infra) Assess autoscaler config for hb-prod-pool — consider faster burst capacity or queue-aware scaling.
- (hana/tara) Customer comms + contract implications.

sam: I'll open incident ticket INC-304210 and include metrics snapshot and rbctl history.

jess: I'll start a trace on prefix-cache growth and correlate with HarborBank request patterns (long context vectors).

mike: Also check whether any scheduled batch jobs for hb-internal-a overlapped with traffic spike — we might need to prevent heavy background jobs during peak windows.

lia: We'll keep fairshare bump for 1 hour as planned. If metrics look stable at +30m, we can step down weight gradually.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-304210 (HarborBank VPC - fairshare saturation -> 429s). Assigned: lia, sam, jess. Priority: P2.

hana: Note for post-mortem: include timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps, and recommended infra + product changes (burst pool, queue-aware autoscaling, tenant job isolation).

tara: I'll set a follow-up CTO sync if legal or contract waiver needed.

lia: Thanks team. Monitoring continues. :thumbsup:

(30m later) sam: 429s steady at <0.5%, queues normal. Leaving bump in place for 15 more minutes then will ramp down. Closing updates in INC-304210.
